question: Which statement is FALSE regarding fundamental rights mentioned in the Indian Constitution ?
option_1: Only Article 20 and 21 can be suspended during emergency
option_3: Some fundamental rights are negative in nature
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only Article 20 and 21 can be suspended during emergency.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• This statement is FALSE because it is the exact opposite of the constitutional position. (मौलिक अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 20 और 21)

 

• Under Article 359, when a National Emergency is in operation, the President can suspend the right to move any court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights (except Articles 20 and 21) — all other Fundamental Rights can be suspended, not just Articles 20 and 21.

 

• Article 20 (Protection in respect of conviction for offences) and Article 21 (Protection of life and personal liberty) are the two rights that cannot be suspended even during an emergency, as per the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978.

 

• Hence the statement as worded ("Only Article 20 and 21 can be suspended") reverses the actual rule and is the false statement asked for in the question.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Rights are enforceable in a court of law (justiciable), unlike the Directive Principles of State Policy.

 

• Some Fundamental Rights are negative in nature, i.e., they restrain the State from doing certain things (e.g., Article 20 prohibits ex-post-facto laws).

 

NOTE

 

• They are justiciable (Option 2): This is a true statement — Fundamental Rights can be enforced through courts under Article 32/226.

 

• Some fundamental rights are negative in nature (Option 3): This is a true statement, e.g., Article 20 and Article 22 impose restraints on the State.

 

• Can be suspended during emergency (Option 4): This is a true general statement — Fundamental Rights (other than Articles 20 and 21) can indeed be suspended during a National Emergency.

question: The Golden Quadrilateral connects which of the following cities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi-Kolkata-Mumbai-Chennai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Golden Quadrilateral (GQ) is a network of highways connecting India's four major metropolitan cities — Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata. (स्वर्णिम चतुर्भुज — दिल्ली-मुंबई-चेन्नई-कोलकाता)

 

• It is the largest highway project in India and the fifth-longest in the world, with a total length of about 5,846 km.

 

• It was launched in 1999 under the National Highways Development Project (NHDP), championed by then Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

 

• The GQ connects the four corners of the country and links the four largest metros, forming a rough quadrilateral shape on the map.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The North-South and East-West Corridors are other major NHDP highway projects, connecting Srinagar to Kanyakumari and Silchar to Porbandar respectively.

 

• The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) is responsible for the development, maintenance and management of national highways including the GQ.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1, 3 and 4: None of these city combinations correspond to the actual Golden Quadrilateral, which is fixed as Delhi-Kolkata-Chennai-Mumbai; the other options list unrelated or partially incorrect city sets.

question: Which of the following government schemes provides subsidised food grains to poor households in India?
option_2: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) was launched in March/April 2020 to provide free/subsidised food grains (rice/wheat) to poor and vulnerable households during the COVID-19 pandemic. (प्रधानमंत्री गरीब कल्याण अन्न योजना — मुफ्त राशन)

 

• Under the scheme, 5 kg of food grains per person per month is provided free of cost, in addition to the regular quota under the National Food Security Act (NFSA), 2013.

 

• It is implemented by the Department of Food and Public Distribution, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution.

 

• The scheme has been repeatedly extended and later merged/integrated with NFSA distribution to continue providing free food grains to about 81 crore beneficiaries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• National Food Security Act, 2013 provides the legal entitlement for subsidised food grains through the Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS).

 

• Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) is another scheme targeted at the poorest of the poor for subsidised food grains.

 

NOTE

 

• Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (Option 1): A skill development scheme, not related to food security.

 

• Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (Option 3): The health insurance component of Ayushman Bharat, providing hospitalisation cover, not food grains.

 

• Atal Pension Yojana (Option 4): A pension scheme for workers in the unorganised sector, unrelated to food grains.

question: Who among the following boxers won the women's lightweight gold medal at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham and received the BBC Emerging Player of the Year Award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nitu Ghanghas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nitu Ghanghas won a gold medal in women's boxing (48 kg category) at the 2022 Commonwealth Games, Birmingham, defeating England's Demie-Jade Resztan in the final. (नीतू घंघस — कॉमनवेल्थ गेम्स 2022 स्वर्ण पदक)

 

• She was honoured with the BBC Indian Sportswoman of the Year 2022 — Emerging Athlete of the Year award for her outstanding performance.

 

• Nitu Ghanghas hails from Bhiwani, Haryana, and trains at the famous Bhiwani Boxing Club.

 

• At the 2022 CWG, India's other boxing gold came from Nikhat Zareen (women's 50 kg, flyweight).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mirabai Chanu (weightlifting) won the main BBC Indian Sportswoman of the Year 2022 award.

 

• Nitu Ghanghas later also won a gold medal at the 2023 World Boxing Championships.

 

NOTE

 

• Nikhat Zareen (Option 1): Won CWG 2022 gold in the 50 kg (flyweight) category, not the category referred to here, and did not receive the BBC Emerging Athlete award.

 

• Lovlina Borgohain (Option 2): An Olympic bronze medallist boxer (Tokyo 2020, welterweight) who did not compete/win gold at CWG 2022 boxing.

 

• Saweety Boora (Option 3): An Indian boxer, but she did not win the CWG 2022 gold medal or the BBC award referred to in this question.

question: Who is called the father of the modern Indian dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uday Shankar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Uday Shankar (1900–1977) is widely regarded as the father of modern Indian dance. (उदय शंकर — आधुनिक भारतीय नृत्य के जनक)

 

• He pioneered a new genre of dance that creatively fused Indian classical dance techniques with Western theatrical and ballet elements, popularising Indian dance on the world stage.

 

• He founded the Uday Shankar India Culture Centre at Almora in 1938 to train dancers in his innovative style.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan and is the elder brother of legendary sitar player Pandit Ravi Shankar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Uday Shankar's wife, Amala Shankar, and son, Ananda Shankar, also made significant contributions to Indian dance and music respectively.

 

• He directed the acclaimed dance-based film Kalpana (1948).

 

NOTE

 

• Ambui Singh (Option 2): Not a recognised figure associated with this title.

 

• CV Chandrasekhar (Option 3): A noted Bharatanatyam exponent and Padma Bhushan awardee, but not called the father of modern Indian dance.

 

• Raja Reddy (Option 4): A well-known Kuchipudi dancer, not associated with this title.

question:
Which of the following statements are correct about Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution ?

A) They are negative in nature.

B) They have moral and political sanctions.

C) They promote the welfare of the rich.

D) They are positive in nature.
solution_text:
The correct answer is B and D.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statements B and D are correct regarding the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). (राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व — सकारात्मक प्रकृति)

 

• Statement B is correct: DPSPs are not legally enforceable in a court of law; they carry only moral and political sanction, unlike Fundamental Rights which are justiciable.

 

• Statement D is correct: DPSPs are positive in nature — they direct the State to take positive action to promote the welfare of the people, unlike Fundamental Rights, which are largely negative (restraining the State).

 

• Statement A is incorrect: DPSPs are positive, not negative, in nature — it is the Fundamental Rights that are largely negative.

 

• Statement C is incorrect: DPSPs aim to promote the welfare of all citizens, especially the weaker sections, not the rich.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• DPSPs are contained in Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Constitution and are inspired by the Irish Constitution.

 

• Though non-justiciable, DPSPs are considered fundamental in the governance of the country, as stated in Article 37.

 

NOTE

 

• C and D (Option 1): Incorrect because C is a wrong statement.

 

• A and B (Option 2): Incorrect because A is a wrong statement.

 

• A and C (Option 3): Incorrect because both A and C are wrong statements.

question: Which of the following festivals is celebrated on the Makar Sankranti day in Assam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Magh Bihu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Magh Bihu, also known as Bhogali Bihu, is celebrated in Assam in the month of Magh (mid-January), coinciding with Makar Sankranti. (माघ बिहू — असम का फसल उत्सव)

 

• It is a harvest festival marking the end of the harvesting season, celebrated with community feasts (Bhoj) and bonfires (Meji).

 

• A distinctive tradition is building a temporary hut called Bhelaghar, which is burnt down on the morning of the festival.

 

• Traditional games like buffalo fighting, egg fighting, and tekeli bhonga (pot breaking) are organised during Magh Bihu.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bohag Bihu (Rongali Bihu) is celebrated in mid-April, marking the Assamese New Year and the onset of the sowing season.

 

• Kati Bihu (Kongali Bihu) is observed in October, a solemn festival marking the completion of sowing/transplanting of paddy.

 

NOTE

 

• Kati Bihu (Option 1): Celebrated in October, not on Makar Sankranti.

 

• Bohag Bihu (Option 3): Celebrated in April, marking the Assamese New Year, not Makar Sankranti.

 

• Raksha Bandhan (Option 4): A pan-Indian festival celebrated in August (Shravan), unrelated to Makar Sankranti.

question: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) was placed in the Guinness Book of World Records for which of the following achievements?
option_1: Opening the largest number of bank accounts in one month
option_2: Opening the largest number of bank accounts in one week
option_3: Opening the largest number of bank accounts in one fortnight
option_4: Opening the largest number of bank accounts in one day
solution_text:
The correct answer is Opening the largest number of bank accounts in one week.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY), launched on 28 August 2014, entered the Guinness World Records for opening the most bank accounts in one week. (जन धन योजना — गिनीज बुक रिकॉर्ड)

 

• As per the record, 1,80,96,130 bank accounts were opened during the week of 23–29 August 2014, as part of the financial inclusion drive.

 

• PMJDY is the National Mission for Financial Inclusion, ensuring access to banking, savings, credit, insurance and pension facilities.

 

• It is administered by the Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• PMJDY accounts come with a RuPay debit card, accident insurance cover, and an overdraft facility.

 

• As of recent years, PMJDY has facilitated the opening of more than 50 crore bank accounts across India.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 (one month, fortnight, one day): All are factually incorrect time-frames; the officially recognised Guinness record is for the one-week period.

question: In May 2022, President Ram Nath Kovind appointed ____ as the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vinai Kumar Saxena.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vinai Kumar Saxena was appointed as the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi by President Ram Nath Kovind in May 2022. (विनय कुमार सक्सेना — दिल्ली के उपराज्यपाल)

 

• He succeeded Anil Baijal, who had resigned from the post.

 

• Prior to this appointment, Vinai Kumar Saxena served as the Chairman of the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC).

 

• As LG of Delhi, he serves as the administrative head of the National Capital Territory of Delhi.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Manoj Sinha is the Lieutenant Governor of Jammu & Kashmir.

 

• Admiral D K Joshi served as the Lieutenant Governor of Andaman & Nicobar Islands.

 

NOTE

 

• Manoj Sinha (Option 1): LG of Jammu & Kashmir, not Delhi.

 

• Admiral D K Joshi (Option 2): LG of Andaman and Nicobar Islands, not Delhi.

 

• Dr Tamilisai Soundararajan (Option 3): Served as the Governor of Telangana and Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry, not Delhi.

question: In which year was Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi born?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1869.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi was born on 2 October 1869 in Porbandar, Gujarat. (महात्मा गांधी — जन्म 1869)

 

• He is popularly known as the Father of the Nation (Rashtrapita) and led India's freedom struggle through the philosophy of non-violence (Ahimsa) and Satyagraha.

 

• His birthday, 2 October, is celebrated in India as Gandhi Jayanti, and is observed globally as the International Day of Non-Violence.

 

• He passed away on 30 January 1948, assassinated by Nathuram Godse.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gandhi's major movements include the Champaran Satyagraha (1917), Non-Cooperation Movement (1920), Civil Disobedience/Dandi March (1930), and Quit India Movement (1942).

 

• His autobiography is titled "The Story of My Experiments with Truth".

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 (1659, 1889, 1879): These are all incorrect years; Gandhi's verified birth year is 1869.

question: Santoor is associated with whom among the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Shivkumar Sharma.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Shivkumar Sharma was the foremost exponent of the Santoor, a trapezoid-shaped hammered dulcimer used in Indian classical music. (संतूर — पंडित शिवकुमार शर्मा)

 

• He is credited with popularising the santoor as a solo classical instrument, having elevated it from a folk instrument of Kashmir to the concert stage.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan (2001) and often performed in the celebrated Shiv-Hari duo with flautist Hariprasad Chaurasia, composing music for several Bollywood films.

 

• He also received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for his contribution to Hindustani classical music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pandit Jasraj was a legendary Hindustani classical vocalist of the Mewati Gharana.

 

• Pandit Bhimsen Joshi was a renowned Hindustani classical vocalist of the Kirana Gharana, and a Bharat Ratna awardee.

 

NOTE

 

• Pandit Jasraj (Option 2): Associated with vocal (Hindustani classical) music, not the santoor.

 

• Pandit Bhimsen Joshi (Option 3): Associated with vocal (Hindustani classical) music, not the santoor.

 

• Hari prasad Chaurasia (Option 4): A legendary exponent of the bansuri (flute), not the santoor.

question: Which type of haploid unicellular eukaryote cells has a diameter of ~10 μm, and about half of their volume is occupied by cup-shaped chloroplasts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chlamydomonas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chlamydomonas is a genus of unicellular, biflagellate, haploid green algae measuring about 10 micrometres in diameter. (क्लैमाइडोमोनास — कप के आकार का क्लोरोप्लास्ट)

 

• About half its cell volume is occupied by a single, large, cup-shaped (cup-like) chloroplast, which is a distinctive identifying feature of this alga.

 

• It reproduces both asexually (by zoospores) and sexually, and is widely used as a model organism in cell and molecular biology, genetics, and photosynthesis research.

 

• It belongs to the class Chlorophyceae (green algae).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chlamydomonas is notable for having a light-sensitive eyespot (stigma) that helps it move towards light (phototaxis).

 

• It is used extensively to study flagellar structure and function and photosynthetic mechanisms.

 

NOTE

 

• Hydrodictyon (Option 1): A colonial green alga forming a net-like ("water-net") coenobium, not a solitary unicellular form with a cup-shaped chloroplast.

 

• Ulva (Option 2): A multicellular, sheet-like green alga ("sea lettuce"), not unicellular.

 

• Oedogonium (Option 4): A filamentous green alga, not unicellular.

question: Which of the following is the product as a result of the process of hydrolysis of orthoclase.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kaolinite.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Orthoclase feldspar is a common rock-forming mineral (potassium aluminium silicate) that, upon hydrolysis (chemical weathering by water), breaks down to form Kaolinite, a type of clay mineral. (काओलिनाइट — ऑर्थोक्लेज़ का जल-अपघटन उत्पाद)

 

• This process is a key example of chemical weathering, where water reacts with the mineral, removing soluble potassium and silica and leaving behind hydrated aluminium silicate clay.

 

• Kaolinite is the primary constituent of china clay/kaolin, widely used in the ceramics, paper, and paint industries.

 

• This weathering process is especially significant in the formation of laterite and clay soils in tropical regions with high rainfall.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Orthoclase is one of the most abundant minerals in the Earth's crust, forming a major component of granite and other felsic igneous rocks.

 

• Other clay minerals like illite and montmorillonite can also form from feldspar weathering under different conditions.

 

NOTE

 

• Limonite (Option 1): A hydrated iron oxide mineral, formed from the weathering of iron-bearing minerals, not orthoclase.

 

• Magnesite (Option 2): A magnesium carbonate mineral, unrelated to orthoclase hydrolysis.

 

• Gypsum (Option 3): A calcium sulfate mineral, typically formed by evaporation of saline water, not by feldspar hydrolysis.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the reasons why the public sector played a dominant role in establishing the Industrial sector in India post-Independence?
option_1: Poor savings capacity of the public
option_2: To avoid generation of private profit
option_3: Absence of large enough market for output
option_4: Lack of adequate capital with private industrialists
solution_text:
The correct answer is To avoid generation of private profit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "To avoid generation of private profit" was NOT a reason for the public sector's dominant role in India's post-Independence industrialisation. (सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र — निजी लाभ रोकना कारण नहीं)

 

• The profit motive is a fundamental driver of private entrepreneurship and capitalism, and the government's industrial strategy was not aimed at suppressing it.

 

• The real reasons for public sector dominance included poor savings and investment capacity of the private sector, an absence of a sufficiently large market for industrial goods, and a lack of adequate capital with private industrialists to undertake large, capital-intensive projects.

 

• This is based on the standard economic-development explanation (as in NCERT's account of the Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956) for why the government took direct responsibility for setting up heavy and basic industries at that time.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 classified industries into three categories based on the role of the state, giving the public sector a dominant position in heavy industries.

 

• The public sector was also expected to prevent the excessive concentration of economic power in a few private hands, though this differs from "avoiding private profit" altogether.

 

NOTE

 

• Poor savings capacity of the public (Option 1): A genuine reason — the private sector lacked sufficient capital for large industrial ventures.

 

• Absence of large enough market for output (Option 3): A genuine reason — limited market size discouraged private investment in heavy industry.

 

• Lack of adequate capital with private industrialists (Option 4): A genuine reason — private industrialists did not have the resources needed for capital-intensive projects.

question: Saurashtra won the Vijay Hazare Trophy 2022 by defeating:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saurashtra won the Vijay Hazare Trophy 2022–23 by defeating Maharashtra by 5 wickets in the final, held at Ahmedabad on 2 December 2022. (विजय हजारे ट्रॉफी — सौराष्ट्र चैंपियन)

 

• This was Saurashtra's third Vijay Hazare Trophy title.

 

• Chirag Jani was Saurashtra's standout performer, and the team's disciplined bowling and batting depth helped seal the win.

 

• The Vijay Hazare Trophy is India's premier domestic List A (50-over) cricket tournament, organised by the BCCI.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Saurashtra reached the final after beating Karnataka in the semi-final of the 2022–23 edition.

 

• The Vijay Hazare Trophy is named after former Indian cricket captain Vijay Hazare.

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 1): Saurashtra beat Karnataka in the semi-final, not the final.

 

• Delhi (Option 2): Not the finalist opponent of Saurashtra in the 2022–23 Vijay Hazare Trophy.

 

• Andhra (Option 3): Not the finalist opponent of Saurashtra in the 2022–23 Vijay Hazare Trophy.

question: 'The Deccan Sabha' was founded by which of the following nationalists?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gopal Krishna Gokhale.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Deccan Sabha was founded in 1896 by Gopal Krishna Gokhale at Poona (Pune) as a more moderate alternative to the Poona Sarvajanik Sabha. (गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले — दक्कन सभा)

 

• Gokhale was a leading Moderate leader of the Indian National Congress and founded the Servants of India Society in 1905 to train national workers for public service.

 

• He is often regarded as the political mentor of Mahatma Gandhi, who called him his guru.

 

• Gokhale advocated constitutional methods, gradual reform, and education as tools for national progress.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gokhale was also instrumental in the passage of the Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms).

 

• He served as a member of the Imperial Legislative Council.

 

NOTE

 

• Pherozeshah Mehta (Option 2): A prominent Moderate leader who founded the Bombay Presidency Association, not the Deccan Sabha.

 

• Surendranath Banerjee (Option 3): Founded the Indian National Association, later merged with the Indian National Congress.

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji (Option 4): Known for the "Drain of Wealth" theory and founding the East India Association; he did not found the Deccan Sabha.

question: Who among the following medieval rulers focused his attention on the construction of sarais (shelter) for the convenience of travellers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sher Shah Suri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sher Shah Suri (r. 1540–1545), founder of the Sur dynasty, focused heavily on building sarais (rest houses) for travellers along his highways. (शेर शाह सूरी — सराय निर्माण)

 

• He constructed the famous Grand Trunk Road (Sadak-e-Azam) connecting Bengal to the Indus, and built sarais at regular intervals along it for the comfort and security of travellers and traders.

 

• These sarais also served as postal relay stations (dak chowki), aiding his efficient communication and administrative system.

 

• Sher Shah Suri is also credited with major reforms in revenue administration and introducing the Rupiya, a silver coin.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun at the Battle of Kannauj (1540) and established Sur rule in North India.

 

• His administrative reforms greatly influenced the later Mughal administration under Akbar.

 

NOTE

 

• Babur (Option 1): Founder of the Mughal dynasty, known for military conquests (Battle of Panipat, 1526), not for sarai construction.

 

• Akbar (Option 3): Known for administrative and religious reforms like the Mansabdari system and Din-i-Ilahi, not specifically for sarai-building.

 

• Humayun (Option 4): Known for his eventful reign and eventual restoration of Mughal power; not particularly noted for sarai construction.

question: A diagonal relationship is found between which pair of the following elements?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Li and Mg.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A diagonal relationship exists between certain elements of Period 2 and elements of Period 3 positioned diagonally to them in the periodic table, and Lithium (Li) and Magnesium (Mg) are a classic example. (विकर्ण संबंध — लिथियम और मैग्नीशियम)

 

• Both Li (Group 1, Period 2) and Mg (Group 2, Period 3) show similar chemical properties due to similar charge/size (ionic potential) ratios, such as forming covalent compounds, similar solubility patterns, and both forming a nitride on burning in nitrogen.

 

• Other classic diagonal relationship pairs include Be and Al, and B and Si.

 

• This similarity arises because diagonal elements have comparable atomic/ionic size and electronegativity, despite being in different groups and periods.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Diagonal relationships are most prominent in the first three groups of the periodic table (Groups 1, 2 and 13).

 

• The diagonal relationship of Be and Al explains why beryllium shows several aluminium-like properties, such as amphoteric oxide formation.

 

NOTE

 

• Be and B (Option 2): Not a recognised diagonal relationship pair; the classic pairing for Be is with Al.

 

• Be and Mg (Option 3): These are both Group 2 elements (same group, adjacent periods), not a diagonal relationship.

 

• Na and Mg (Option 4): These are Period 3 elements in adjacent groups of the same period, not a diagonal relationship pair.

question: Which of the following is NOT included in 'Operating Surplus'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Wages in cash.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Operating Surplus is a component of factor income and is defined as the sum of Rent + Interest + Profit — it does NOT include Wages (which falls under Compensation of Employees). (परिचालन अधिशेष — मजदूरी शामिल नहीं)

 

• In National Income Accounting, factor incomes are broadly classified as Compensation of Employees (wages/salaries, in cash and kind) and Operating Surplus (property and entrepreneurial income), plus Mixed Income of Self-Employed.

 

• Rent, Interest and Profit together constitute Operating Surplus, since they represent returns to property and entrepreneurship.

 

• Wages (in cash or kind) are treated separately as Compensation of Employees, since they are the return to labour, not to property/entrepreneurship.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Compensation of Employees = Wages and salaries in cash + Wages and salaries in kind + Employers' contribution to social security schemes.

 

• Domestic Factor Income = Compensation of Employees + Operating Surplus + Mixed Income of Self-Employed.

 

NOTE

 

• Rent (Option 1): A genuine component of Operating Surplus.

 

• Profit (Option 2): A genuine component of Operating Surplus.

 

• Interest (Option 3): A genuine component of Operating Surplus.

question: The 2028 Olympic Games will take place in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Los Angeles.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2028 Summer Olympic Games are scheduled to be held in Los Angeles, USA, from 14 to 30 July 2028. (लॉस एंजिलिस — 2028 ओलंपिक)

 

• This will be the third time Los Angeles hosts the Summer Olympics, having previously hosted them in 1932 and 1984.

 

• Los Angeles was officially awarded the Games by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in 2017, as part of a dual-award process alongside Paris (2024).

 

• The 2024 Summer Olympics were held in Paris, France.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Brisbane, Australia is set to host the 2032 Summer Olympics.

 

• The 2036 Olympics host is yet to be finalised, with several countries, including India, expressing interest.

 

NOTE

 

• Paris (Option 1): Hosted the 2024 Summer Olympics, not 2028.

 

• Tokyo (Option 2): Hosted the 2020 Summer Olympics (held in 2021 due to COVID-19), not 2028.

 

• Amsterdam (Option 4): Hosted the 1928 Summer Olympics, not any recent or upcoming edition.

question: Who among the following personalities won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2021 for their contribution to the 'Chhau' dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhuvan Kumar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bhuvan Kumar was conferred the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 2021 (awards for 2019–2021 announced together in February 2023) for his contribution to the Chhau dance. (छऊ नृत्य — भुवन कुमार)

 

• Chhau is a semi-classical Indian dance form, blending martial, tribal and folk traditions, practised in the states of Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal, each with its own distinct style (Mayurbhanj, Seraikella and Purulia Chhau).

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award is India's highest recognition given to practising artists in the fields of music, dance and drama.

 

• The award carries a citation, an angavastram and a cash prize.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chhau dance was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, established in 1952, is India's national academy for music, dance and drama, headquartered in New Delhi.

 

NOTE

 

• Bijay Kumar Jena, Rabindra Atibudhi and Trilochan Mohanta (Options 1, 2 and 4): These are all names of artists, but none of them received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2021 for Chhau dance as recognised in the source material.

question: Which of the following is NOT a monetary policy instrument of RBI?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Government Spending.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Government Spending is an instrument of Fiscal Policy, controlled by the Government/Ministry of Finance, not a monetary policy instrument of the RBI. (सरकारी व्यय — राजकोषीय नीति का साधन)

 

• Monetary policy is formulated and implemented by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) through its Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) to control money supply, inflation and credit in the economy.

 

• Key RBI monetary policy instruments include the Bank Rate, Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR), and Open Market Operations (OMO).

 

• Government Spending and Taxation are core tools of fiscal policy, aimed at influencing aggregate demand and economic growth through the government's budget.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), headed by the RBI Governor, decides the repo rate to maintain price stability while supporting growth.

 

• Fiscal policy tools also include public debt management and deficit financing, distinct from monetary tools.

 

NOTE

 

• Bank Rate (Option 2): A genuine monetary policy instrument — the rate at which RBI lends long-term funds to commercial banks.

 

• Open Market Operations (Option 3): A genuine monetary policy instrument — RBI's buying/selling of government securities to regulate liquidity.

 

• Cash Reserve Ratio (Option 4): A genuine monetary policy instrument — the minimum percentage of deposits banks must hold as reserves with the RBI.

question: Which of the following is NOT a component of investment?
option_2: Money spent on purchasing shares of a company
option_3: Machinery and equipment employed by a firm
option_4: Inventories of raw materials stocked by a firm
solution_text:
The correct answer is Money spent on purchasing shares of a company.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In economics (National Income Accounting), "Investment" refers to addition to the physical/real capital stock of the economy, and money spent on purchasing shares is a financial transaction, not real investment. (निवेश — केवल वास्तविक पूंजी निर्माण)

 

• Buying shares merely represents a transfer of ownership of existing financial assets between individuals/entities — it does not add to the productive capacity of the economy and is therefore excluded from GDP-based investment.

 

• Genuine (real) investment includes fixed investment (machinery, buildings, residential/non-residential construction) and inventory investment (change in stock of raw materials, semi-finished and finished goods).

 

• This distinction is important in National Income Accounting, where only real capital formation counts towards Gross Domestic Capital Formation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gross Domestic Capital Formation (GDCF) = Fixed Capital Formation + Change in Stocks (Inventories).

 

• The purchase of second-hand goods or existing financial assets like shares/bonds is also excluded from investment/GDP calculations to avoid double counting.

 

NOTE

 

• Addition to residential construction (Option 1): A genuine component of fixed investment (real capital formation).

 

• Machinery and equipment employed by a firm (Option 3): A genuine component of fixed investment.

 

• Inventories of raw materials stocked by a firm (Option 4): A genuine component of investment (inventory/stock investment).

question: Which of the following places in India experiences the lowest temperature?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Leh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Leh, located in the Union Territory of Ladakh at a high altitude in the cold desert region of the trans-Himalayas, experiences the lowest temperatures among the given places, often dropping well below -20°C in winter. (लेह — लद्दाख का शीत मरुस्थल)

 

• Being situated at an elevation of about 3,500 metres above sea level, Leh has an extreme continental climate with very cold, dry winters and mild summers.

 

• Nearby areas like Drass, also in Ladakh, are among the coldest inhabited places in India, sometimes referred to as the "Gateway to Ladakh" and known for extremely low winter temperatures.

 

• The other options — Jaisalmer (hot desert), Munnar (hill station with a moderate climate) and Bundelkhand (semi-arid plateau) — do not experience such extreme cold.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ladakh, including Leh, is often called a "cold desert" due to its low precipitation combined with extremely cold winters.

 

• Drass, in Ladakh, has recorded temperatures as low as -45°C, making it one of the coldest inhabited places in the world.

 

NOTE

 

• Jaisalmer (Option 1): Located in the Thar (hot) Desert, Rajasthan; experiences very high summer temperatures, not extreme cold.

 

• Munnar (Option 3): A hill station in Kerala with a pleasant, moderately cool climate, not as extreme as Leh.

 

• Bundelkhand (Option 4): A semi-arid plateau region in Central India with hot summers and moderately cool winters, not comparable to Leh's extreme cold.

question: What is the name of the 87th element on the periodic table that has no known biological role because it has a half-life of only 22 minutes?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Francium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Francium (Fr) is the element with atomic number 87 and is one of the rarest naturally occurring elements on Earth. (फ्रांसियम — परमाणु क्रमांक 87)

 

• Its most stable isotope, Francium-223, has a half-life of only about 22 minutes, making it extremely radioactive and short-lived.

 

• Because it decays so rapidly and exists in such minute quantities in nature (formed via the decay of actinium), it has no known biological role and is never found in appreciable amounts.

 

• Francium is an alkali metal, placed in Group 1, Period 7 of the periodic table, below caesium.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Francium was discovered in 1939 by French scientist Marguerite Perey, after whom it is named (France).

 

• It is considered the second most electropositive element after caesium, though its extreme rarity and radioactivity limit practical study and use.

 

NOTE

 

• Meitnerium (Option 1): A synthetic superheavy element with atomic number 109, not 87.

 

• Dubnium (Option 2): A synthetic superheavy element with atomic number 105, not 87.

 

• Seaborgium (Option 3): A synthetic superheavy element with atomic number 106, not 87.
